samples.summary: `Array.isArray(thread.comments)` guard is false for every real Yorkie thread, so `listThreads`/`findThread` skip all stored threads — the whole comments API reads empty and every reply/resolve/delete 404s
samples.evidence: `listThreads` (line 116) and `findThread` (line 129) both bail with `!Array.isArray(thread.comments)`. This repo documents the opposite of the assumption in `packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet-charts.controller.ts:67-70`: "`detachYorkieValue` does not save it either — it branches on `Array.isArray`, which is false for an array proxy". Inside `withDocument`, `map[threadId].comments` is a Yorkie array proxy, so both guards evaluate to `continue`/`undefined` for genuine threads. Consequences: `GET .../comments` returns `{threads: []}`; `tabIdOfThread` (comments.controller.ts:709-713) never finds a tab, so `mutateMap` throws `NotFoundException`; the flat doc/pdf path's `findThread(doc.getRoot().comments, threadId)` (comments.controller.ts:463) also 404s. Every reply, resolve, unresolve, thread delete and comment delete therefore fails against a real document. Note the same file uses `Array.from(t.comments ?? [])` at line 99 (the proxy-safe form the frontend uses) — the guard is inconsistent with it. The unit tests cannot catch this because `comment-ops.spec.ts` and `comments.controller.spec.ts` both build threads as plain JS objects.

samples.summary: `copyThread` detaches the anchor with `detachYorkieValue`, which this repo documents as turning nested Yorkie array proxies into `{createdAt, movedAt}` CRDT metadata — corrupting docs-range `posRange` in the API response
samples.evidence: `copyThread` does `anchor: (detachYorkieValue(t.anchor) ?? {}) as AnyAnchor`. `packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet-charts.controller.ts:62-70` explicitly says to use `unwrapJson`, "never a spread and never `detachYorkieValue`", because `detachYorkieValue` "branches on `Array.isArray`, which is false for an array proxy, so the array comes back as `{createdAt, movedAt}` CRDT metadata". A `docs-range` anchor's `posRange` is a pair (array) of TreePos structs, so listing a word-processor document's threads returns a mangled anchor rather than the stored positions. The spec at comment-ops.spec.ts only exercises a plain-object `pdf-region` rect, so it does not cover this.

samples.summary: Notification `preview` is the raw comment body, so mention tokens `@[name](7)` leak into the notification dropdown instead of being flattened to `@name`
samples.evidence: `planCommentNotifications` sets `preview: comment.body` (line 572) and `preview: thread.comments[0]?.body ?? ''` (line 550). The frontend rule this claims to mirror runs the body through `mentionBodyToPlainText` first (`packages/frontend/src/components/comments/notify.ts:35-37`), and `mentions.ts:119-123` documents that step exists precisely so "the raw token must not leak". `NotificationService.sanitizePreview` only strips control characters and truncates, so the token survives to the client.

samples.summary: An unknown `layoutId` is silently accepted and produces a 'blank' slide instead of a 400
samples.evidence: `add` only checks that `layoutId` is a non-empty string. `MemSlidesStore.resolveLayout` (packages/slides/src/store/memory.ts:172-174) falls back to `getLayout(layoutId)`, and `getLayout` (packages/slides/src/model/layout.ts:196-198) returns `BUILT_IN_LAYOUTS[0]` (`'blank'`) for any unrecognised id. A typo in `--layout` therefore silently creates a blank slide whose `layoutId` is rewritten to `'blank'`, with no error — despite the controller shipping a `layouts` catalog specifically so the id is checkable.

samples.summary: `parsePdfAnchor` validates each rect component in 0..1 individually but never that the rectangle stays on the page (`x+w<=1`, `y+h<=1`)
samples.evidence: The loop at lines 672-680 only rejects a component `< 0 || > 1`. `{ x: 0.9, y: 0.9, w: 0.9, h: 0.9 }` passes and stores an anchor whose region extends far past the page, which the PDF comment layer renders with `left: x*100%` / width beyond the page box. The docblock and the spec ("refuses a rectangle outside the page") only cover the `w: 2` case.

samples.summary: `parseImages` accepts a row-zero A1 anchor such as "A0" because `parseRef` does not validate the row number
samples.evidence: `parseImage` validates the anchor by calling `parseRef(anchor)` and only catching a throw. `parseRef` (packages/sheets/src/model/core/coordinates.ts:323-340) only throws when no digit follows the letters; `"A0"` yields `{ r: 0 }` without throwing, so an image is stored anchored to a non-existent row 0. The comment path guards against this downstream (`sheetCellAnchor` rejects because `rowOrder[-1]` is undefined), but the image path stores it verbatim.

samples.summary: `deleteComment` validates the comment id only inside `doc.update`, so a normal "unknown comment id" request throws out of the CRDT update callback — the pattern the sibling images controller deliberately avoids
samples.evidence: `mutateMap` validates only the *thread* before entering `doc.update` (lines 449-467). `applyDeleteComment` returns `'not_found'` for an unknown `commentId`, and the resulting `NotFoundException` (line 419) is thrown from inside the `doc.update` callback. `packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet-images.controller.ts:104-107` states the rule being broken: "Checked *before* `doc.update` rather than inside it: throwing from within the update leaves an aborted change on a document this request should not have touched at all." An unknown comment id is ordinary caller input, not a race.

verdict.reason: The guard exists exactly as claimed at comment-ops.ts:116 and :129, and both are fed live Yorkie proxies: yorkie.service.ts:36-61 hands the callback a real attached yorkie.Document, and comments.controller.ts:221/235/463/711 pass doc.getRoot() sub-objects into listThreads/findThread with no detach step. The repository itself documents the failing premise in two places (worksheet-charts.controller.ts:67-70 and worksheet-filter-pivot.controller.ts:71, restated in worksheet-filter-pivot.controller.spec.ts:88-95): Array.isArray is false for a Yorkie array proxy, consistent with the SDK proxying a CRDTArray rather than an Array exotic object. So thread.comments is an array proxy and both guards reject every genuine stored thread. The same file's proxy-safe Array.from(t.comments ?? []) at comment-ops.ts:99, mirrored by all three frontend stores (yorkie-comment-store.ts:100, pdf-comment-store.ts:77, yorkie-worksheet-comments.ts:51) and the unguarded Object.values walk at yorkie-comment-store.ts:283, shows the intended form. No caller-side guard prevents this; on the contrary the guard is the thing producing the empty read and the 404s (comments.controller.ts:450, :463-465, :484). Unit tests cannot expose it because comments.controller.spec.ts:26-34 uses a plain-object fake root. Blocking under the correctness rubric: a wrong condition that breaks the entire comments API core flow (list returns empty; reply/resolve/unresolve/delete all 404) on the normal production path.

verdict.reason: The code is present as described: comment-ops.ts:98 detaches the anchor with detachYorkieValue, whose Array.isArray branch (yorkie-json.ts:168) is documented in this same repo as false for a Yorkie array proxy, causing the array to come back as {createdAt, movedAt} CRDT metadata (worksheet-charts.controller.ts:67-70; worksheet-filter-pivot.controller.ts:69-72; lessons doc 20260827:13-21, with a real-Document regression suite at worksheet-filter-pivot.controller.spec.ts:88-144). A docs-range anchor genuinely holds a nested array: types/comments.ts:31 types posRange as TreePosStructRange and yorkie-comment-store.ts:164-198 writes that pair into the CRDT (its own comment at :81-87 warns against serializing it). The path is reachable on live proxies: comments.controller.ts:232-239 lists a 'doc' document's threads via listThreads(doc.getRoot().comments) -> copyThread (comment-ops.ts:119), and copyThread is also used on resolve (comments.controller.ts:486). No guard filters docs-range anchors before copyThread; only thread *creation* on docs is refused (comments.controller.ts:265-270). The existing spec (comment-ops.spec.ts:170-190) uses a plain object from buildThread, so it cannot catch it. Wrong/corrupted anchor data returned on a normal API path is a correctness defect in this lens.

finding.summary: `Array.isArray(thread.comments)` is false for a Yorkie array proxy, so `listThreads`/`findThread` reject every thread actually stored in the CRDT
finding.evidence: `listThreads` (comment-ops.ts:116) and `findThread` (:129) both gate on `!Array.isArray(thread.comments)` and skip/return-undefined when it fails. When the map comes from a live Yorkie root (`doc.getRoot().sheets[tabId].comments[id]`), `thread.comments` is a Yorkie ArrayProxy whose proxy target is a `CRDTArray`, not a JS array — this repo states that explicitly twice: worksheet-filter-pivot.controller.ts:71 ("`Array.isArray`, which is false for a Yorkie array proxy") and worksheet-charts.controller.ts:68. Consequently, against a real document: `GET .../comments` returns `{threads: []}`, and `reply` / `PATCH` / `DELETE :threadId` / `DELETE :threadId/comments/:commentId` all 404 via `findThread`/`tabIdOfThread` (comments.controller.ts:463, :711). Every unit test in comments.controller.spec.ts / comment-ops.spec.ts feeds plain JS objects, so the whole feature passes CI while being non-functional in production. The frontend stores never use this guard — they use `Array.from(t.comments ?? [])` (yorkie-worksheet-comments.ts:51), which works on the proxy.

verdict.reason: The guard exists exactly as described at comment-ops.ts:116 and :129, and the maps it inspects come from live Yorkie proxies (yorkie.service.ts:46 builds a real Document; comments.controller.ts:221/235/449/463/483/711 read off doc.getRoot()). The repository itself documents that Array.isArray is false for a Yorkie array proxy (worksheet-charts.controller.ts:67-69, worksheet-filter-pivot.controller.ts:71-74, docs/tasks/archive/2026/08/20260827-v1-worksheet-review-fix-lessons.md:16), and every working reader avoids the check by using Array.from (comment-ops.ts:99, yorkie-worksheet-comments.ts:51, yorkie-store.ts:1057-1065). No guard or caller makes the path unreachable — copyThread's Array.from runs only after the isArray gate already rejected the thread. Result: list returns empty and reply/resolve/delete 404 against real documents, while unit tests using plain objects pass. Real, reachable, breaks a core flow.

finding.summary: `applySetResolved` unconditionally `delete`s `resolvedAt`/`resolvedBy` on reopen; deleting a key that is not present on a Yorkie object throws, so `PATCH {resolved:false}` on a never-resolved thread can 500
finding.evidence: comment-ops.ts:214-224 runs `delete thread.resolvedAt` / `delete thread.resolvedBy` whenever `resolved === false`, with no existence check. Yorkie's object proxy `deleteProperty` routes to `CRDTObject.deleteByKey` → `RHTPQMap.deleteByKey`, which raises `fail to find <key>` when the key was never set. The route accepts `{resolved:false}` on any thread (comments.controller.ts:368-379), including one that was never resolved or one reopened twice — cases the editor UI cannot produce (its reopen control only exists on resolved threads), which is why the identical frontend code at yorkie-worksheet-comments.ts:142-143 never hits it. Result: a 500 on an idempotent reopen.

verdict.reason: Code is present exactly as described: comment-ops.ts:215-224 unconditionally `delete thread.resolvedAt` / `delete thread.resolvedBy` whenever the engine returns no resolution fields, which per packages/sheets/src/comment/thread.ts:78-89 is always the case for `resolved === false`. Threads created by createThread (thread.ts:11-28) never carry those keys, so the delete targets an absent key. The path is reachable: comments.controller.ts:358-379 accepts `{resolved:false}` on any thread with no current-state guard, and mutateThread/mutateMap (controller:439-489) pass a live Yorkie object proxy obtained inside `doc.update`, so the delete goes through Yorkie's deleteProperty trap rather than a plain object. No upstream guard, early return, or state check exists anywhere; the only tests covering applySetResolved (comment-ops.spec.ts:102-114) use plain objects where `delete` is a no-op, so they cannot expose it. I could not read the @yorkie-js/sdk sources (node_modules absent) to disprove the throw-on-missing-key behavior, and per instructions that residual uncertainty keeps the finding. In-lane (unguarded crash / broken idempotency on a normal API path), so not out-of-scope.
